junction.name: Springfield Boulevard & Horace Harding Expressway, New York City

claims.text: Springfield Boulevard & Horace Harding Expressway had 108 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 11 pedestrians injured, 0 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $7.4 million a year.
35% of crashes here involved a truck or bus, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
34% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.
20% of crashes here had “following too closely” recorded as a contributing factor, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was hit on the center back end and a vehicle was going straight ahead in 34% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 13% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).
Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading west in 37% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 18% at the city's priority junctions (found by the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 3.2 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.1 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.7 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $577,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for LONG ISLAND EXP (I 495) (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Springfield Boulevard, Horace Harding Expressway (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 23, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 11.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11; the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 23, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 11
Subject: Request for safety study at Springfield Boulevard & Horace Harding Expressway

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

We write to ask each agency to carry out a safety study at Springfield Boulevard & Horace Harding Expressway on the roads it is responsible for, and to make the fixes below where warranted.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 288 crashes, including 108 injury crashes. 11 pedestrians were injured and 0 cyclists were injured. No one was killed. This junction is on the city’s priority list. In dollar terms, the harm is $7.4 million per year in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). No recent safety work is recorded in this period.

On the roads you own, please consider:

* longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals) – expected to prevent about 5.9 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $2,012,000 in harm per year, subject to a site check for an entry on yellow or red.
* reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders) – expected to prevent about 3.2 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,109,000 in harm per year, subject to a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

The city’s measurement of a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green) found where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain. This also needs a site check for a turning movement.

Please let us know the findings and next steps for each road.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 4215 (longer yellow signal times)
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 1410 (reflective backplates on the traffic signals)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
- NearMissLens NML-Bench T11: before/after study of the city's own installs (validation/BENCH.md)
- Road owners: the registry's road-inventory layer (see the engineer report's receipts)
